title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. We work in a linear group scheme, apparently GL(M) with M of rank 2: the next page uses det λ = λ² for scalars. There are:
- nilpotent elements N_0, N_1 (N_i² = 0);
- additive one-parameter subgroups ε_i(λ) = 1 + λN_i;
- two elements ρ, σ, each conjugating N_0 into N_1, with centralizers (tori) T_ρ, T_σ;
- groups B̃_i, defined by the condition v N_i v^{-1} = det(v)·N_i. These are the subgroups of the normalizer of the line spanned by N_i on which the character by which v acts on N_i equals det.

On the previous page Grothendieck reduced a compatibility condition (formula (69), coming from the 'loop equations' (33)–(35)) to the identity
(**) int(ε_1)(v) = v·ε_1(1/μ − 1), for v in B̃_1 and μ = det v.

This page verifies (**).
1. Write ε_1 = 1 + N_1, so ε_1^{-1} = ε_1(−1) = 1 − N_1.
2. A first attempt expands (1+N_1)v(1−N_1). It contains a sign slip (+N_1vN_1 instead of −N_1vN_1) and is crossed out.
3. The clean version: ε_1 v ε_1(−1) = v ε_1(1/μ − 1). Since ε_1 is additive, this is equivalent to ε_1 v = v ε_1(1/μ).
4. That gives v + N_1v = v + μ^{-1}vN_1, i.e. N_1v = μ^{-1}vN_1, i.e. v N_1 v^{-1} = μN_1.
5. This is exactly the defining condition of B̃_1, so (**) holds identically.

Consequence. The rule u ↦ ([u,ρ], [u,σ], det u) (commutators) defines a morphism (66) from B̃_0 to H_{ρ,σ}, the scheme of solutions of the system (33)–(35). Here det u plays the role of the 'cyclotomic' parameter μ.

Grothendieck then asks whether (66) is an isomorphism, starting with injectivity. He observes that [u,ρ] = [u',ρ] iff u u'^{-1} lies in the centralizer T_ρ. Hence the monomorphism question reduces to T_ρ ∩ B̃_0 (and likewise T_σ ∩ B̃_0).

The next page completes this:
- Assuming T_σ ∩ T_ρ = G_m (the centre), the intersection is G_m ∩ B̃_0 = μ_2, since a scalar λ satisfies λN_0λ^{-1} = N_0 while det λ = λ².
- So (66) is not a monomorphism; its kernel is μ_2 and it factors through B̃_0/μ_2.

Overall, this is a step in determining the solution scheme of a linearized 'equation des lacets'. It plausibly belongs to a GL_2 / SL_2(Z)-type model of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-like relations: two elements ρ, σ with a unipotent N, and a parameter μ acting like the cyclotomic character. The aim is to parametrize the solutions by a Borel-type group modulo μ_2.
errors: The crossed-out expansion of (1+N_1)v(1−N_1) has a sign error: it should be v + N_1v − vN_1 − N_1vN_1, not + N_1vN_1. Grothendieck abandoned it and redid the computation correctly via ε_1 v = v ε_1(1/μ).

The question 'is (66) an isomorphism?' gets a negative answer on the next page (kernel μ_2). The injectivity criterion stated here implicitly needs (66) to be read as a group-like map with kernel; the reduction to T_ρ ∩ B̃_0 is fine, but strictly the kernel is T_ρ ∩ T_σ ∩ B̃_0.

ideas.what: Verification that int(1+N)(v) = v(1+(μ^{-1}−1)N) is equivalent to vNv^{-1} = det(v)N, using additivity of the one-parameter unipotent subgroup.
ideas.modern_name: Elementary computation with a unipotent one-parameter subgroup normalized by a Borel-type subgroup (character twist by det)

ideas.what: Parametrizing solutions (ρ', σ', μ) of the system (33)–(35) by commutators with elements u of a Borel-type group B̃_0 with μ = det u, and testing whether this parametrization is an isomorphism (kernel governed by the centralizers T_ρ, T_σ).
ideas.modern_name: Describing a solution scheme of GT-type ('loop') equations in a linear representation as a homogeneous space under a Borel-type subgroup modulo μ_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; the GT formalism is usually credited to Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara
ideas.where_published: Only the general program appears, in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche; this specific computation is not known to be published.

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether the commutator map B̃_0 → H_{ρ,σ} onto solutions of the loop equations (33)–(35) is an isomorphism. Injectivity is resolved on the next page (kernel μ_2), but the surjectivity part of 'est-ce un isomorphisme ?' is not settled on this page. The question would be a concrete description of a 'linearized' solution scheme of the loop equations.
missed.quote: de B̃_0 dans l'ens des solutions de (33) à (35), est-ce un isomorphisme ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If (33)–(35) are a rank-2 linear shadow of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations, a full determination of the solution scheme would be a small explicit model of GT-type torsors in GL_2. Its value depends on identifying the equations, which are only partially visible here.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a routine verification inside an ongoing computation. Its interest lies in the unpublished context: an explicit linear model of the 'équation des lacets', with det playing the cyclotomic role. Nothing on the page itself is a new result.
transcription_corrections: In the crossed-out line the term is written '+ N_1vN_1' (a sign slip by Grothendieck); the correct expansion would have '−'.
'ε_1^*(-1)' is ε_1(−1) = ε_1^{-1}; the asterisk is a stray mark.
'On trouve donc un morphisme' — the image appears to read 'On trouve donc un morphisme' after a crossed-out 'monomorphisme'.
'dans l'ens des solutions' = 'dans l'ensemble des solutions'.
The kernel criterion reads: 'signifie que u u'^{-1} ∈ T_ρ' (the 'Γ' read by the machine is likely a stray mark or '∈').
